headline.en: Three liars who can't quit. Different roots. Same dead end.
headline.zh: 三种戒不掉的骗子。不同的根，同一条死胡同。

subtext.en: What's the difference between not stopping, not changing, and never stopping in the first place?
subtext.zh: '停不下来'、'改不了'、'从一开始就一直在' — 这三件事的区别是什么？

definition.en: Beyond correction — someone you can warn, punish, coach, or beg, and the behavior comes back unchanged.
definition.zh: 无法被纠正 — 你可以提醒、惩罚、教导、恳求他，行为还是会原样回来。

etymology.en: From Latin in- (not) + corrigere (to set straight) — itself com- (together) + regere (to rule, guide). Same regere gives us 'regulate,' 'direct,' 'regime,' and 'regent.'
etymology.zh: 拉丁 in-（不）+ corrigere（弄直）— corrigere 又由 com-（合）+ regere（管、引导）构成。同一个 regere 还给了我们 regulate、direct、regime、regent。

sentences.en: He's an incorrigible interrupter — three coaches and two reviews later, he's still mid-sentence over everyone else.
sentences.zh: 他是个屡教不改的打断王 — 换了三个教练、做了两次评估，他还是在每个人话头上抢着说。

sentences.en: Some kids are sweetly incorrigible — you tell them no, they smile, and you watch them try it again.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子是甜甜的'屡教不改' — 你说不行，他们一笑，然后你眼睁睁看他们又试了一次。

mnemonic.en: In + Corrigere = NOT + STRAIGHTEN. The door is bolted from the inside. No coach is getting in.
mnemonic.zh: In + Corrigere = 不 + 弄直。门是从里面锁的。再厉害的教练也进不去。

question.en: Stubborn and incorrigible both refuse to change. Which is harder to live with?
question.zh: Stubborn（固执）和 incorrigible（屡教不改）都是不肯变。哪个更难相处？

answer.en: Stubborn refuses on the issue. Incorrigible refuses being CORRECTED — even when they agree the behavior is wrong, the next time happens anyway.
answer.zh: Stubborn 是在某件事上不让步。Incorrigible 是抗拒'被纠正'本身 — 哪怕他承认行为不对，下一次还是会再来。

anecdote.en: In Victorian schools 'incorrigible' was a formal label — once stamped on a student's record, no teacher tried to teach them anymore. The word didn't just describe the kid. It was the school giving up.
anecdote.zh: 在维多利亚时代的学校里，'incorrigible'是一个正式标签 — 一旦盖在学生档案上，再没有老师愿意教他们。这个词不只是在描述孩子，它其实是学校在举手投降。

definition.en: Settled into a habit so old it's part of the person — they don't fight it, they don't notice it, they just keep doing it.
definition.zh: 习惯已经老到长进骨头里 — 他不抵抗，也不察觉，就是一直在做。

etymology.en: From Latin inveteratus = 'aged into' — in- (into) + vetus (old). Same vetus gives us 'veteran' (old soldier) and 'veterinarian' (originally a doctor of old draft animals).
etymology.zh: 拉丁 inveteratus = 长进岁月里 — in-（进入）+ vetus（老）。同一个 vetus 给了我们 veteran（老兵）和 veterinarian（最初指给老牲口看病的医生）。

sentences.en: She's an inveterate note-taker — even at the coffee machine, the notebook is open.
sentences.zh: 她是个根深蒂固的笔记控 — 哪怕站在咖啡机旁，笔记本都是翻开的。

sentences.en: He's an inveterate optimist — twenty years of bad luck haven't changed his face.
sentences.zh: 他是个根深蒂固的乐观主义者 — 二十年的霉运也没改过他脸上的表情。

mnemonic.en: Vetus = OLD. Inveterate = aged INTO the person. Not a behavior they have. A behavior they ARE.
mnemonic.zh: Vetus = 老。Inveterate 是习惯长进了这个人。不是他'有'这个行为，而是他'就是'这个行为。

question.en: Habitual and inveterate are close. What's the texture difference?
question.zh: Habitual 和 inveterate 很接近。在质感上有什么差别？

answer.en: Habitual = does it regularly. Inveterate = has done it so long it's identity, not action. You can interrupt a habit. You'd have to rewrite a person to interrupt the inveterate.
answer.zh: Habitual = 经常做。Inveterate = 做得太久，已经变成身份而不是动作。你可以打断一个习惯，但要打断'根深蒂固'，你得重写一个人。

anecdote.en: Mark Twain once described himself as an 'inveterate procrastinator' — and meant it half as a confession, half as pride. The funny part is that he wrote thirty books anyway. Inveterate doesn't always mean lost. Sometimes it means: this is who I am, and I'll work around it.
anecdote.zh: 马克·吐温曾经形容自己是'根深蒂固的拖延者' — 一半是认错，一半是带点自豪。有意思的是他还是写了三十本书。'根深蒂固'不总意味着完蛋。有时候它意味着：这就是我，我会绕着它继续走。

definition.en: Persisting over a long time, with no clean ending — chronic problems don't explode. They quietly never go away.
definition.zh: 长期持续，没有干净的结尾 — 慢性的问题不会爆发，而是安静地一直不走。

etymology.en: From Greek chronos = 'time.' Same chronos gives us 'chronicle' (record of time), 'chronology,' 'anachronism' (out of time), and 'synchronize' (same time).
etymology.zh: 希腊词根 chronos = 时间。同一个 chronos 给了我们 chronicle（编年史）、chronology（年代学）、anachronism（错时）、synchronize（同步）。

sentences.en: Their meetings have chronic agenda creep — one item starts on time, the rest stretches into forever.
sentences.zh: 他们的会议有慢性议程蔓延症 — 第一条按时讨论，剩下的一拖再拖。

sentences.en: Chronic lateness isn't a habit. It's a quiet message about whose time matters.
sentences.zh: 长期迟到不是个习惯 — 是一个安静的信号，告诉别人谁的时间更重要。

mnemonic.en: Chronos = TIME. Chronic = something that has time on its side. It outlasts your patience to wait it out.
mnemonic.zh: Chronos = 时间。慢性 = 站在时间这一边的事情。它能耗光你等它结束的耐心。

question.en: In medicine, what's the difference between chronic and acute?
question.zh: 在医学里，chronic 和 acute 有什么区别？

answer.en: Acute = sharp and short — onset fast, ends fast. Chronic = long and slow — no clear start, no clear end. Most modern suffering is chronic.
answer.zh: Acute = 急性 — 起得快、走得也快。Chronic = 慢性 — 没有明确的起点，也没有明确的终点。现代人大多数的痛苦都是慢性的。

anecdote.en: Greek myth had two gods of time. Chronos was clock time — the slow, accumulating river of it. Kairos was the right moment — the perfect now. Most chronic problems exist because we keep waiting for the kairos to fix what's already cost us years of chronos.
anecdote.zh: 希腊神话里有两个时间之神。Chronos 是钟表时间 — 缓慢累积的那条河。Kairos 是恰当的那一刻 — 完美的'现在'。大多数慢性问题之所以一直在，是因为我们总在等那个'恰当的时机' — 来修复早已花掉我们好多年 chronos 的事。

setup.en: Both can't quit. But one resists fixing. The other doesn't see the need.
setup.zh: 两人都戒不掉。但一个抗拒被修，另一个根本看不到要修。

leftLine.en: You can't fix it from outside.

leftMnemonic.en: In-Corrigere = NOT-CORRECT · the door bolted from inside.
leftMnemonic.zh: In + Corrigere = 不 + 弄直 · 门从里面锁着。

rightLine.en: It's just what they DO. Always has been.
rightLine.zh: 这就是他们的'做法'。一直都是。

rightMnemonic.en: Vetus = OLD · the habit aged into the person.
rightMnemonic.zh: Vetus = 老 · 习惯长进了这个人。

closing.en: One can't be changed. The other doesn't know change is an option.
closing.zh: 一个无法被改变。一个根本不知道'改变'这个选项存在。

reflection.en: Habits don't break when you push them — they break when you finally see them clearly. The hardest part of changing isn't the will. It's the seeing.
reflection.zh: 习惯不会因为你用力推就断 — 它们要等你真正看清它们的那一刻才断。最难的不是意志，是看见。

gloss.en: To set right — com- (together) + regere (rule, guide). The verb that 'incorrigible' refuses.
gloss.zh: 弄直、改过来 — com-（合）+ regere（管、引导）。屡教不改的人，正是拒绝这个动词。

usage.en: Correcting someone's grammar is easy. Correcting their reasoning is the brave kind.
usage.zh: 纠正别人的语法很容易。纠正他们的思路，才是有勇气的那种纠正。

gloss.en: To keep something within a rule — from regula (a straight rod, a ruler), itself from regere (to rule).
gloss.zh: 把某件事控制在规则之内 — 来自 regula（直尺、规则），而 regula 又来自 regere（管）。

usage.en: A wise body regulates emotion the way a thermostat regulates heat — not by killing it, but by setting a range.
usage.zh: 一个清醒的人调节情绪，就像恒温器调节温度 — 不是消灭它，而是给它一个范围。

gloss.en: A system of rule — government, training plan, or treatment schedule. Same regere as 'regulate.'
gloss.zh: 一套被规则约束的系统 — 政府、训练计划、治疗方案皆可。和 regulate 同根。

usage.en: Every new regime promises change. Most just rearrange who gets the perks.
usage.zh: 每个新政体都承诺变革，大多数只是重新分配一下'谁享有特权'。

gloss.en: To guide straight — di- (apart, distinctly) + regere (guide). Both the adjective ('straight, frank') and the verb ('to lead').
gloss.zh: 笔直地引导 — di-（分开、明确地）+ regere（引导）。既是形容词（笔直、直率），也是动词（指引）。

usage.en: A direct answer takes one breath. Most of us take ten and call it diplomacy.
usage.zh: 一个直接的回答只用一口气。我们大多数人要用十口气，再把它叫做'外交辞令'。

gloss.en: One who rules in place of another — the present participle of regere, literally 'ruling.'
gloss.zh: 代替他人统治的人 — regere 的现在分词，字面意思是'正在管的人'。

usage.en: Every regent rules with someone else's name on the throne — and someone else's risk on the line.
usage.zh: 每一位摄政者，王座上挂着的是别人的名字 — 而冒险的，也是别人的命。

gloss.en: An old hand — one who has been at it long enough to count. Direct from vetus, 'old.'
gloss.zh: 老手 — 在这件事上做了够久、值得算数的人。直接来自 vetus（老）。

usage.en: A veteran isn't just someone old at the job — it's someone who has paid in mistakes.
usage.zh: 老手不只是在这行干了很久的人 — 是用错误付过学费的人。

gloss.en: Originally a doctor of old draft animals — vetus (old). The aged horses and oxen needed their own physician.
gloss.zh: 最初是给老牲口看病的医生 — vetus（老）。上了年纪的马和牛需要自己的医生。

usage.en: A good veterinarian reads animals like a translator reads a foreign poem — slowly, with respect.
usage.zh: 好的兽医读动物，像译者读一首外语诗 — 慢慢地，带着尊重。

gloss.en: A record of events in the order they happened — from chronos (time). Same root as 'chronic.'
gloss.zh: 按发生顺序记录的事件 — 来自 chronos（时间）。和 chronic 同根。

usage.en: Every family has a private chronicle — the version that gets told at funerals, not parties.
usage.zh: 每个家庭都有一部私人编年史 — 是葬礼上讲的那个版本，不是聚会上的那个。

gloss.en: The arrangement of events by time — chronos + logos (study). The science of figuring out what happened in what order.
gloss.zh: 把事件按时间排开 — chronos + logos（学问）。研究'什么事按什么顺序发生'的学问。

usage.en: Memory has its own chronology — the order that matters isn't the calendar's.
usage.zh: 记忆有自己的时间顺序 — 它在意的顺序，并不是日历上的那个。

gloss.en: Something out of its proper time — ana- (against) + chronos. A flip phone in a 2025 movie. A Roman with a wristwatch.
gloss.zh: 时代错置 — ana-（反）+ chronos。2025 年的电影里出现翻盖手机；古罗马人戴手表。

usage.en: Some of our laws are anachronisms — written for a world that no longer exists.
usage.zh: 我们有些法律是时代错置的产物 — 为一个早已不存在的世界写的。

gloss.en: To make two times line up — syn- (together) + chronos (time).
gloss.zh: 让两个时间对齐 — syn-（一起）+ chronos（时间）。

usage.en: Heist movies always have the watch-synchronizing scene because precision is the only thing standing between plan and disaster.
usage.zh: 劫案电影里总会有对表的镜头 — 因为精确，是计划和灾难之间唯一的那道墙。

gloss.en: Living in the same time — con- (together) + tempus (time). Latin's tempus is the cousin of Greek's chronos: same idea, different ancestor.
gloss.zh: 生活在同一个时代 — con-（一起）+ tempus（时间）。拉丁的 tempus 是希腊 chronos 的表亲 — 同一个概念，两个祖先。

usage.en: Two contemporaries can live in totally different worlds — same year, different centuries inside their heads.
usage.zh: 两个同时代的人，可以活在完全不同的世界 — 同一年，可脑子里却各自处在不同的世纪。
